title: Discovery
description:
Something the player can come to understand. The unit of progression: the game has no experience points, so a discovery moving up its ladder is what advancement means.

This is a definition, not a record of play. Canon says what CAN be known and what it takes to know it; whether a particular player has got there lives in their save, never here.

name.description: What the completed entry is called. The player will not see this until they have earned it.

discipline.description: Which section of the diary this files under, and which knowledge track it advances.

subject.description: The canon entity this is about -- a species, a settlement, an event, an artifact. A discovery is nearly always a way of coming to understand something that already exists.

found_at.description: point_of_interest ids where this can be encountered. More than one is fine and desirable: meeting the same thing twice in different places is how a pattern becomes visible.

levels.description: The ladder from noticing to understanding, in order. Index is the level: 0 unknown, 1 observed, 2 identified, 3 explained, 4 connected, 5 significant. Not every discovery needs all six -- a shell may stop at identified, while an ecological relationship earns the full climb. Each rung is what the diary shows once reached, so it is written for the player.

entry.description: What the diary reads at this level. Varuna's voice, and it should sound less certain at the lower rungs.

requires.description: What must be true to reach this rung: other discovery ids, vocabulary ids, a tool, an npc consulted. Empty means it follows from the level below.

conditions.description: When this rung can be reached at all, if the world has to cooperate.

answers.description: field_question ids this contributes evidence toward. A question usually needs several.

related_discoveries.description: Discoveries that become more meaningful once this one is held. The 'connected' rung is built from these.

notes.description: Reference fact for the canon reader. Not shown to the player.
